tasks.short: Lead excavation training sites and train field participants.

steps.what: Choose excavation training objectives and assess actual site and participant needs
inputs: actual excavation site conditions
actual participant experience and training requirements

steps.what: Prepare chosen excavation method illustrations, instructions and practice materials
inputs: chosen site-specific excavation training approach
current controlled method illustrations

steps.what: Lead actual field training sites and teach staff, students and volunteers excavation methods
inputs: checked saved site-specific training materials
actual site and participants
outputs: actual teaching, observed practice and participant feedback

steps.what: Write and check actual field-training observations and retain assigned outcome notes
inputs: actual teaching, observed practice and participant feedback
outputs: checked saved actual field-training outcome notes

tasks.design: Configure reuse of selected excavation illustrations and method sections in {DOCS}/{LMS}. Keep actual site adaptation, complete material checks, field instruction and observed outcome recording; internal saving stays ungated and earns no saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stable method illustrations are repeatedly assembled into site materials.
tasks.enabler_now: Native section reuse can avoid this assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Excavation teaching depends on real contexts, fragile evidence and participant behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor stops an apparently competent technique that would destroy context.
tasks.altitude: Less training-material assembly; field teaching stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: reusable method illustrations can reduce training preparation while field excavation teaching remains human.

assumptions: Provisional shares: five of20 material points are repeated illustration/section assembly; fifteen include actual adaptation and complete checking. Native saves remain within retained time. Existing reuse gets no new credit.

Method owners supply current section id, revision and applicability; instructor supplies actual site constraints and participant observations. Missing sources are obtained manually. Outcomes only follow real practice; assigned notes are conditional on actual ownership, otherwise drop and reweight. No inferred competence or invented external report.
unknowns: How much method material already exists as reusable sections?
research_questions: Does reuse preserve site-specific excavation cautions?

incremental.description: Maintain excavation method illustrations and applicability labels.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High removes5 stable illustration-assembly points minus0.5 upkeep=4.5. Low: an unfamiliar site needs new examples and cautions, leaving only2 stable tool-handling illustration points removed, minus0.5=1.5. Site assessment, teaching and actual outcome records remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct participatory research and co-design work systems and environments.

steps.what: Conduct actual participatory action research and capture agreed observations with community participants
inputs: actual community or organisation questions
actual agreed research access and participation conditions
outputs: actual consent-compatible field observations and participant statements

steps.what: Assess actual work with participants and co-design work systems, technologies and environments
inputs: actual consent-compatible field observations and participant statements
actual participant priorities and constraints
outputs: actual co-design choices, dissent and agreed design rationale

steps.what: Draft the assigned research and work-system design account from actual agreed material
inputs: actual consent-compatible field observations and participant statements
actual co-design choices, dissent and agreed design rationale
outputs: source-linked draft research and design account

loop.purpose: Draft an account of actual observations and co-design choices
loop.input: researcher-checked shareable field notes and actual co-design rationale
loop.output: source-linked draft preserving disagreement and attribution restrictions
loop.check: Researcher checks meaning, omitted dissent, power relationships, confidentiality and whether recommendations were actually agreed
loop.stop: Unclear permission, missing source or two failed revisions returns section to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Test native report sections first; varied field narratives and dissent require semantic checking beyond fixed fields

steps.what: Complete and check the whole internal account and retain its final version
inputs: source-linked draft research and design account
actual consent-compatible field observations and participant statements
outputs: checked saved final internal research and design account

tasks.design: Keep actual participatory research and work-system co-design human, including field-note capture. After native report-section reuse is tested, use a bounded draft in {DOCS} only for researcher-checked, permitted observations; retain complete final checking and an ungated ordinary internal save.
tasks.previous_blocker: A faithful account must be written from varied observations and actual participant decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-constrained drafting can reduce repeated descriptive typing.
tasks.still_hard: Power, consent, disagreement and meaningful participation cannot be inferred from notes.
tasks.human_edge: The researcher surfaces a participant objection that a tidy summary would erase.
tasks.altitude: Less descriptive drafting; field access, interpretation and co-design stay human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: constrained drafting can assist an account from checked field notes while participatory interpretation and confidentiality checks remain human.

assumptions: Provisional boundary includes an actually assigned internal research/design account, not a new report. Five of20 drafting points represent descriptive typing removed after retained semantic review. Field observation, capture, co-design and complete final checks keep all their time.

Researcher produces actual notes with date, context, source permission and attribution restrictions during s1; participant choices arise only in s2. Missing context or permission is clarified manually. No free transcript, fabricated consensus or new participant labour. Actual separate publication or delivery requires its own mapped review/send route and gets no saving here.
unknowns: Can the actual notes be processed under the research agreement?
Which account does the researcher actually own?
research_questions: Does the draft preserve dissent and restricted attribution without new clarification work?

incremental.description: Maintain permitted-source boundaries and check draft attribution/meaning failures.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High removes5 descriptive drafting points minus1 upkeep=4. Low: a contested redesign needs almost all interpretation and narrative written afresh; only2 points describing agreed existing work are removed, minus1=1. Research, co-design and complete final checking remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and test theories about past cultures.

steps.what: Frame cultural-origin and development questions and choose candidate explanations
inputs: actual research questions
existing cultural evidence and unresolved interpretations

steps.what: Locate and read actual cultural evidence and prior theory sources
inputs: candidate theories and test questions
actual evidence catalogues and source papers
outputs: located and read relevant evidence set

steps.what: Develop and test cultural theories against evidence and competing explanations
inputs: candidate theories and test questions
located and read relevant evidence set
outputs: actual theory tests, interpretations and limitations

steps.what: Write and check the actual theory-testing record and save it internally
inputs: actual theory tests, interpretations and limitations

tasks.design: Configure current evidence-catalogue and source links in {DOCS}/{DATA_PLATFORM}. Reduce repeated source navigation while retaining theory formation, substantive reading, testing and the full written interpretation record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence and prior interpretations may be dispersed across catalogues.
tasks.enabler_now: Native source metadata can reduce locating work without deciding cultural meaning.
tasks.still_hard: Sparse and biased evidence can support competing explanations.
tasks.human_edge: The researcher identifies an untestable explanation and states the limit.
tasks.altitude: Less source navigation; theory judgement stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source indexes can reduce evidence navigation but do not establish cultural theories.

assumptions: Provisional source20 contains three locating points removed; seventeen reading/source-selection points remain. Existing search/runtime earns no new credit. Written theory reasoning and its ordinary save are fully retained without self-approval.

Archive and catalogue owners supply actual source id, provenance, dating uncertainty, version and permitted-access link. Missing metadata requires manual source review. Researcher produces actual tests and interpretations; no novel evidence is inferred.
unknowns: Are relevant source catalogues already indexed together?
research_questions: Can current links avoid duplicate sources while preserving dating uncertainty?

incremental.description: Maintain cultural-evidence source links and provenance labels.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High removes3 repeated locating points minus0.4 upkeep=2.6. Low: a theory about a poorly documented culture needs new manual archive searches; only1 known-source locating point disappears, minus0.4=0.6. Scientific reasoning, reading and written theory tests stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Research, survey and assess sites of past societies.

steps.what: Choose specific site research questions and an appropriate survey or assessment method
inputs: actual site research need
actual access and research constraints
outputs: chosen site questions and assessment method

steps.what: Locate and inspect existing site records, maps and prior survey evidence
inputs: chosen site questions and assessment method
actual site catalogues and spatial records
outputs: located and inspected existing site evidence

steps.what: Conduct actual site research and surveys and capture real observations
inputs: chosen site questions and assessment method
located and inspected existing site evidence
actual site conditions
outputs: actual site observations, measurements and provenance

steps.what: Assess actual findings against the research questions and interpret site limitations
inputs: actual site observations, measurements and provenance
located and inspected existing site evidence

steps.what: Write and check actual site findings and retain the internal assessment record
inputs: actual interpreted site assessment
actual site observations, measurements and provenance
outputs: checked saved actual site assessment record

tasks.design: Configure site-identity links to actual maps and prior survey sources in the spatial {DATA_PLATFORM} and {DOCS}. Reduce locating work while retaining physical survey, fresh observation capture, interpretation and assigned written findings; same-system save time is unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing site evidence can be hard to locate consistently.
tasks.enabler_now: Native spatial/catalogue indexes can link real site identifiers and sources.
tasks.still_hard: Site conditions and preservation bias require direct assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The researcher notices a contextual relationship not captured in a map.
tasks.altitude: Less searching for prior evidence; fieldwork and assessment remain human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native spatial and catalogue links can reduce locating existing site sources while field surveys require actual observation.

assumptions: Provisional source20 includes five repeated site/source locating points; substantive inspection remains. Existing native indexes earn no new saving. Fresh written findings are split from fieldwork and fully retained, without invented reporting overhead.

Catalogue owners supply actual site id, coordinates/reference system, source date, provenance and access restrictions. Unmatched site identities or missing records require manual search. Researcher captures actual measurements and context in s3; no digital record is treated as a new observation. Any actual statutory report/send lies outside this internal assessment boundary and must be separately mapped if assigned.
unknowns: How complete are the actual site catalogue and coordinate references?
research_questions: Can source links match sites without collapsing uncertain or overlapping locations?

incremental.description: Maintain site-to-source identity links and access labels.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High removes5 existing-record locating points minus0.5 upkeep=4.5. Low: a previously unrecorded site needs manual archive work; only1 broad-area map locating point is removed, minus0.5=0.5. Actual surveys, observation capture, interpretation and written findings keep their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce selected preparation and descriptive writing around unchanged field and interpretive work.
role.ambitious_version: Current evidence and faithful draft accounts support people who retain field and community judgement.
